how: We read the website of every Las Vegas wedding videographer listed on Lazo (90 listings, 72 sites reachable) and set aside the ones that are not really in the wedding business: corporate video houses and production studios, video guestbook and photo booth rentals, and one photo-video outfit listed ten times under different names. What is left is a shortlist of vendors who say clearly what they do, show their work, and tell you how they work. Verified Lazo vendors come first. Nobody paid to be here, and this is not a ranking: Lazo ranks only on reviews from couples who booked.
ask: Will you record the vows and toasts on a lapel mic or a feed from the DJ, not just the camera's audio?
How long until the highlight film and the full ceremony edit arrive, and is raw footage available?
If part of the day is outdoors at Red Rock or the Strip, do you handle the filming permits and the wind and heat on the equipment?

picks.name: Tree of Life Films & Photos
picks.blurb: A married duo making elopement films and photos for adventure-ish couples across Las Vegas, California, Utah and Arizona. Tree of Life started after the two got their own wedding film and remembered how hard it was to find one that reflected the couple.

picks.name: Saffron Sky Films
picks.blurb: Saffron Sky Films is a destination photo and video studio based in Henderson that serves Las Vegas, California and beyond. The team describes its films as cinematic renditions rather than standard wedding filming, built to be revisited.

picks.name: Pablo Zanardi Wedding and Elopement Photo Video
picks.blurb: Pablo Zanardi films and photographs weddings and elopements with digital, 35mm, Polaroid and Super 8, choosing the medium per wedding. Hundreds of couples since 2018, a rock-and-roll sensibility, and almost ten years based in Las Vegas.

picks.name: Lomax Wedding Films
picks.blurb: Lomax Studios makes wedding films and photography from the same creative vision from the start, so the feeling of the day matches across both. Founder and creative director Casey Lomax leads the studio out of Las Vegas and travels wherever the story is.

picks.name: M Place Productions
picks.blurb: M Place Productions is a boutique photography and cinematography team whose shooters have each trained with owner Matthew, so the style holds across the roster. The price page lists add-ons plainly, including drone coverage at $350 per hour with a two-hour minimum and raw footage delivered on a hard drive.

picks.name: MaxPhotoLV
picks.blurb: MaxPhotoLV has more than 20 years of wedding photography and cinematic videography in Las Vegas, Henderson and Summerlin, with multi-camera coverage among its services. The same team also works private events, corporate functions and entertainment productions.

picks.name: Eugene Kim Photography
picks.blurb: Cinematic wedding photography and film by one artist is Eugene Kim's pitch, for traditional weddings, adventure elopements or both. A three-person team based in San Francisco and Las Vegas, with more than a thousand couples photographed and pricing kept deliberately simple.

picks.name: JCS Photo Video Productions
picks.blurb: Jack Vosburgh started JCS Photo Video Productions in 1987 as a mobile wedding photography and video studio. It still covers Las Vegas, North Las Vegas, Henderson, Boulder City, Pahrump, Laughlin and Mesquite, with lighting and sound as part of the production.

picks.name: Zoltan Wedding Photography & Videography
picks.blurb: Zoltan is a Las Vegas wedding photographer and videographer making timeless photography and films for weddings, elopements and celebrations. The site is built as a curated collection of real Las Vegas weddings, which is the best way to judge the work.

picks.name: ViVA
picks.blurb: ViVA Media Co. is a veteran-owned Las Vegas photo, video and drone company covering weddings, events, corporate work and limo tours. The site promises gallery delivery within 72 hours, and photo booth rentals come from the same team.
